title: Digit Product Minus Digit Sum
statement:
You get a positive integer n. Multiply all of its decimal digits together, add all of its decimal digits together, and return product − sum.

The result can be negative or zero.

examples.why: The 0 makes the product 0, while the sum is still 8. So the answer is negative.
With one digit, product and sum are both 7.

hints: How do you get the last digit of a number without turning it into a string?
n % 10 is the last digit, and Math.floor(n / 10) drops it. Repeat until n is 0.
Keep two running values: a product that starts at 1 and a sum that starts at 0. Update both with every digit.

explain.intuition:
This is a warm-up for digit loops. n % 10 peels off the last digit, and integer division by 10 shifts the rest to the right. Every digit passes through once, so you can update a product and a sum together.

The only trap is the starting values: the product must start at 1 (the identity for multiplication), the sum at 0. A single 0 digit makes the product 0, which is fine and correct.
steps: While n > 0: take d = n % 10, multiply it into prod, add it to sum, then set n = floor(n / 10).
pitfalls: Starting the product at 0, which makes every answer equal to −sum.
Using n / 10 in JavaScript without Math.floor, which never reaches 0 cleanly and adds fractional digits.
Skipping zero digits as if they did not count. A 0 digit really does make the product 0.

solutions.title: Through the digit string
solutions.idea: Turn the number into a string and fold over its characters.

solutions.title: Peel digits with % and /
solutions.idea: Take the last digit with n % 10, drop it with integer division, and update both totals as you go.

followups: n arrives as a string with a million digits. What overflows, and how would you report the answer modulo 10^9 + 7?
Count how many numbers from 1 to N have product equal to sum. Which technique avoids checking each number?
lcTitle: Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits of an Integer
